nodes.label: Zero non-ASCII substitution coverage
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c15-substitution-contracts-and-wiring [ses_f1d0c10b3ffeO3kN4t4OClREBE].md:L2031] **Does any existing test use a non-ASCII value? NO.** Not one. I read all 354 lines. Every string literal in the file is ASCII: `"Test Snippet"`, `"Test Content"`, `"//manual"`, `"//cursor"`, `"Before#{cursor}After"`, `"//trail"`, `"//clip"`, `"Clip: #{clipboard}"`, `"//sc"`, `"//img"`, `"//input"`, `"#{input:}"`, `"//escaped"`, `"snapshot"`, `"base64data"`, `"ZmFrZWltYWdl"`, `"existing-session"`. The only two non-ASCII scalars are `\u{0}` (`:330`, used as a **rejection trigger**, not a value) and the assertion that `LITERAL_HASH` must **not** appear (`:350`). The zero-width space U+200B inside `ESCAPED_HASH_OPEN` is only ever asserted as an internal sentinel to be absent — never as a user value. Given the reported symptom is *variable values coming out corrupted*, this is the headline gap.

nodes.label: Escaped-hash shielding is value-side only
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c15-substitution-contracts-and-wiring [ses_f1d0c10b3ffeO3kN4t4OClREBE].md:L2093] - **Escaped `#{`** — the shielding mechanism is value-side, not template-side. `ESCAPED_HASH_OPEN` is defined at `/home/belajarcarabelajar/Proyek/Snipset/apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/variable.rs:28` as `"\u{200B}LITERAL_HASH\u{200B}"`, written by `escape_hash_open` (`:31-33`) and read back by `restore_escaped_hash_open` (`:37-39`). The doc comment at `:22-27` states it shields *captured content* (OCR / clipboard entries), and a grep confirms `escape_hash_open` is **not called from `evaluator.rs`**. So a template's own `#{clipboard}` is not rewritten before the gates run. **DISPROVEN** for the template-side-escaping miss.

nodes.label: inject_file has no allocation-failure guard
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - h08-windows-cf-hdrop-invariant [ses_f08b44315ffe6sFnX4Uf2EpKQc].md:L2462] 1. **No allocation-failure guard.** `inject_file.rs:74-106`: if `GlobalAlloc` fails (L74) or `GlobalLock` returns null (L76), the code does **not** return — it falls through to L109 and presses **Ctrl+V with the user's pre-existing clipboard contents still live**, pasting whatever was already there into the target app. `EmptyClipboard` (L93) and `SetClipboardData` (L98) results are both discarded, so the same hazard applies to a failed `SetClipboardData` (clipboard left emptied → paste inserts nothing). The sibling `inject_image.rs:104-108` **does** have this guard (`if !image_set { error; clear flag; return; }`); `inject_file.rs` does not. Note the flag *is* eventually cleared on these paths (L153), so it is a wrong-paste hazard, not a permanent-flag-leak.

nodes.label: is_target_terminal recheck is load-bearing
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - h08-windows-cf-hdrop-invariant [ses_f08b44315ffe6sFnX4Uf2EpKQc].md:L2337] 1. **It is not a pure no-op.** It is a live foreground-window query, so a focus change between L86 and L26 makes the internal value the authoritative one. The internal check is the load-bearing one; the caller-side check at L86 is only a fast-path routing optimization. **Do not delete L26 during a "dedupe" refactor** — `engine/injection.rs:234, 276, 281, 289, 294, 302, 356, 376` all call `inject_file_attachment` through the `ClipboardService` trait without any caller-side check, so L26 is the *only* guard on those paths.
